answer: Gate rewards on proof-of-personhood: a privacy-preserving issuer verifies each living human once and signs a nullifier; the ledger accepts one agent registration per nullifier, so a cheap mirror of the key shares the same identity's payout. The voyage from one operator to N distinct identities needs N real humans' credentials, cost roughly linear in N with no compute shortcut. Splitting fails while each identity's lifetime reward stays below one credential's street price; a whole grove of farmed accounts earns one share. Limit: a bribed issuer mints ghosts.
